summary: Asparagus with nori butter, developed during a stage at Canlis: butter infused with nori over very low heat for 5 minutes then rested 15, brushed on blanched asparagus and reheated 3 minutes at 500°F, with a miso-lemon sauce and garnishes; serves 4 as a side, and can be prepped a day ahead.
glance: 6 tablespoons butter infused with 1 sheet nori, strained
24 medium-thick stems, blanched until crisp-tender and shocked
faq: What does nori butter taste like?
It brings umami intensity and a slightly sweet funkiness that pairs beautifully with asparagus.
Do I have to make it this complicated?

No: the garnishes are nori strips, sesame seeds, Maldon, miso-lemon sauce, finely diced blanched lemon zest and chive tips, but you can just toss the asparagus with the nori butter and salt for a delicious side.
How do I make the nori butter?
Melt the butter in a small skillet, tear the nori sheet into pieces and infuse over very low heat for five minutes, allow to rest 15 more minutes, then strain through a fine mesh.
How do I blanch the asparagus?

Cut to uniform length, remove the little random leaves, and blanch in well-salted water until crisp-tender and bright green (the tip of a knife goes in easily with a hint of resistance), then shock in an ice bath.
Can I do it ahead?

All of the prep can be done up to a day in advance; when ready to serve, reheat the butter and brush it on the blanched asparagus and heat in a 500°F oven for about 3 minutes. The author learned it during a two-week stage at Canlis, which serves a version with sauce gribiche.

summary: Pear and gouda salad with a vinaigrette made from the liquid of cryo-pickled onions: romaine hearts, toasted pepitas, shaved aged gouda, pear slices cut at the last minute and pickled onions tossed with olive oil dressing; gluten-free, serves 4 in 15 minutes once the onions are made a day ahead.
glance: 15 minutes if you have the cryo-pickled onions
2 tablespoons pickling liquid, 5 tablespoons olive oil, salt
faq: What are cryo-pickled onions?
An easy, unusual pickling method from the author's cookbook: the onions go right in the salad and the pickling liquid makes the vinaigrette. You must make the onions at least a day in advance.
What gouda should I buy?
The best aged gouda you can afford: the good stuff is at least one year old, with a slightly crystalline texture and pronounced nutty flavor.
Why add ginger?
The author loves how the subtle flavor of fresh ginger works with the pear (it comes from the pickled onions' liquid).
How do I keep the pear from browning?
Slice the peeled pear into 16 pieces just before serving.
How do I dress it?

Whisk the pickling liquid, olive oil and salt (it doesn't need to fully emulsify), then start with half the dressing and add more so the leaves are nicely coated but not drenched. For a more elegant presentation, chill four plates and serve as a composed salad.

summary: Pan-fried polenta with chickpea-peperonata stew, roasted and seared king oyster mushrooms and fig puree, the entree from a City Fruit benefit dinner at Cafe Flora: cold polenta slabs fried golden, mushrooms roasted at 450°F, with a fig puree base; serves 4.
glance: 8 slabs of cold leftover polenta, about 6 x 2 x 3/4 inches, pan-fried until golden on both sides
6 king oysters halved on the diagonal, roasted at 450°F until very tender then seared
1 cup fig puree (or fig spread thinned with boiling water)
faq: What was the occasion?

A five-course benefit dinner at Cafe Flora for City Fruit, a Seattle organization that harvests thousands of pounds of fruit from trees that would otherwise go to waste, donating it to food banks and selling some to local restaurants, and teaching pruning classes. Every course used city-harvested fruit.
What if I don't have fig puree?

Dilute a tasty fig spread with boiling water to a saucy consistency. The author has been coming around to sweet components in savory dishes, which is especially popular in Moroccan cuisine; City Fruit's puree had a rich, raisiny, winey flavor.
Why king oyster mushrooms?

They're the author's favorite backstop when he can't find wild mushrooms: available year-round and often a terrific bargain at Asian groceries. His first choice would have been lobster mushrooms, though chanterelles would also be delicious.
What is the chickpea stew?
A batch of his peperonata (slow-roasted peppers stewed with sofrito) with 1/2 pound of dried chickpeas cooked separately until very tender (or one 15-ounce can in a pinch), heated in a saucepan.
How do I finish the mushrooms?
Toss with olive oil and roast until very tender, then sear in a very hot skillet for a minute for extra flavor.

summary: Gougeres with blue cheese and rosemary: a choux paste of water, butter, salt and flour beaten with 4 eggs, rosemary and mild blue cheese, piped into 2-inch puffs and baked 10 minutes at 400°F then 15 at 375°F, pierced to release steam; yields 30, based on Alice Waters' recipe.
glance: 400°F for 10 minutes, then 375°F for 15 minutes until golden brown and crisp
1 cup water, 6 tablespoons butter, 1 cup flour, 4 eggs
6 ounces mild blue cheese such as Bleu d'Auvergne, plus rosemary
faq: What are gougeres?

Pronounced "goo-zherz": a simple choux paste (pate a choux) dough with cheese mixed in, then baked. There's no chemical or yeast leavening: they rise from steam and the structure created by gluten and eggs. The same dough, minus the cheese, makes eclairs, beignets and cream puffs.
How do I make the dough?

Heat the water, butter and salt until the butter melts without boiling, dump in the flour at once and stir vigorously until the dough pulls away from the pan and one more minute, cool 3 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time (each will seem not to incorporate, keep stirring hard), then the rosemary and cheese.
Why pierce them after baking?
Remove from the oven and pierce each with a sharp knife to let out the steam so they don't get soggy.
How many does it make?

The author doubled Alice Waters' recipe (which says 20 large or 40 small) and got only 30 large, so the recipe is listed doubled. Figure 1-2 per person for a bread basket or appetizers with cocktails.
Can I reheat them?
They taste best fresh out of the oven, but you can reheat at 375°F for about 3 minutes. Other cheeses and herbs also work.

summary: Celery soup with fregola sarda or Israeli couscous: onion and diced celery sauteed 4 minutes, simmered 10-12 minutes in plain water with the toasted pasta, finished with lemon juice and shoyu, and garnished with Parmesan, raw celery and celery leaves; 20 minutes, serves 4 modest servings.
glance: 1/2 cup fregola sarda or Israeli couscous (pan-toast the couscous first), 4 cups water, 10-12 minutes
grated cheese, thinly sliced inner celery rib, celery leaves
faq: What is fregola sarda?
A small, round, toasted pasta from Sardinia with a delightful nutty flavor. If you can't find it, use Israeli couscous, pan-toasted first, or pearled barley, which needs more cooking time.
Can I use regular couscous?
No: don't confuse the tiny-grained Moroccan couscous, which doesn't work in this soup, with the larger Israeli couscous.
Why does the broth start with just water?
So that you can really taste the celery. The garnish adds both thinly sliced raw celery and celery leaves to emphasize the flavor and add a hint of crunch.
What does shoyu do?
A tablespoon of shoyu with the lemon juice, stirred in at the end, adds savory depth to the simple broth.
What do I serve with it?
The author suggests Brussels sprout gratin for a perfect comfort-food dinner, in shallow soup plates like your grandmother's.

summary: Tofu in the style of Southeast Asian steamed fish: firm tofu slabs scored deeply in both directions to expose surface area, sauced with soy, mirin and ginger and sealed with lemongrass, jalapeno, scallion and bell pepper in parchment or banana leaf packets, baked about 20 minutes at 400°F; serves 4.
glance: 20 ounces firm or extra-firm, 8 slabs about 1/2 inch thick, scored in both directions
soy, mirin, ginger, lemongrass, jalapeno, scallion, bell pepper, long pepper, lime
faq: Why score the tofu?

Marinating in soy-based sauce, even overnight, barely penetrates: when you cut in, the sauce has gone about 3 microns deep. Freezing and thawing helps but makes tofu spongy. Scoring a 1/2-inch slab deeply in both directions increases the surface area, and reminded the author of fish.
Why wrap it in parchment?

Steaming in a packet (often a banana leaf) is popular in Vietnamese, Thai and Indian cuisines, and the aromatic steam bursts out when diners open their own. The author wanted a vegetarian dish that captured the "heart-poundingly delicious" steamed fish concept; individual packets also let you customize the spice level for each person.
What is long pepper?

It was imported to ancient Rome along with the black pepper we use today, with a similar flavor but hotter and with an intense floral note. If you don't want to track it down, use a mixture of black pepper and cayenne and maybe coriander seed.
How do I prepare lemongrass?

Use only the lower 3 inches of a stalk, remove the bottom tip and outer layers until you reach a slightly tender inner shoot, pound it well with something heavy like a rolling pin, then mince it. Do a good job or you'll end up with woody bits.
Did he pre-marinate?
No. His first try left the tofu in a heavy soy marinade for days and it was far too salty; the better version just scores and wraps it with classic seasonings.

summary: Seared tofu poke, a vegetarian take on Hawaiian poke: tofu rectangles fried 5 minutes until well browned and tossed in a sesame oil, kecap manis, shoyu and ginger sauce with green onion and jalapeno, served over bean sprouts and fresh seaweed (or rehydrated hijiki); vegan, 20 minutes, serves 4.
glance: 8 ounces firm, 2 x 1 x 1/2 inch, fried about 5 minutes until well browned
1 cup ogo, limukohu, hijiki or mixed seaweed
Vegan and gluten-free (check the soy sauces)
faq: What is poke?

Pronounced POH-keh, the Hawaiian equivalent of sashimi or crudo: typically raw fish seasoned with soy and onion, often on a bed of seaweed. This vegetarian version uses seared tofu, which pairs perfectly with those Asian flavors.
What seaweed should I use?

Any fresh variety thin enough to eat raw. Look for Sea Tangle brand in the refrigerated section of health-food stores or Asian groceries, a fresh mixed seaweed packed in salt that you simply rinse. The other option is dried hijiki, which must be rehydrated.
How do I make the tofu taste good?
Pat it thoroughly dry and fry in a single layer in a very hot, preferably cast-iron skillet until well browned on both sides, then toss in the sauce and rest 3 minutes.
Can I serve it chilled?
Yes, poke can be served at room temperature or chilled.
Any variations?
Use kaiware radish sprouts instead of mung bean sprouts for a spicy variation, and add sriracha or wasabi to the sauce.

summary: White asparagus salad with watercress and Romano: raw white asparagus peeled and sliced paper-thin on the bias, tossed just before serving with cipollini or shallot, watercress and a grapefruit vinaigrette (2 parts oil to 1 part juice) and topped with pecorino romano shavings; serves 1, multiply as needed.
glance: 2 parts olive oil, 1 part fresh grapefruit juice, 1/2 teaspoon zest, salt
2 thick white spears, tough ends snapped off, peeled, sliced thin on the diagonal
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the cheese
faq: Why raw white asparagus?

Thinly sliced raw white asparagus has a nice vegetable sweetness and crunch. The author developed the salad testing recipes for an asparagus tasting menu at his first Herbivoracious dinner party, using California spears until local asparagus arrived.
How should I prepare the asparagus?
Snap off the tough ends, peel the spears, and slice very thinly on a diagonal bias. Cut the cheese with a vegetable peeler.
How do I fix the vinaigrette?
The author found it needed more citrus flavor: grapefruit is a lot less acidic than lemon, so next time he'd use more of the zest and a little bit of neutrally flavored vinegar.
When do I toss it?
Just before serving, toss the asparagus, onion and greens with the dressing, arrange on a plate and top with cheese, finishing salt and black pepper.
What other greens work?
Watercress, arugula or mache.

summary: Paella cakes with manchego and candied Seville orange peel: saffron and smoked paprika short-grain rice cooked, cooled, bound with egg, pressed into panko, pan-fried crispy and topped with melting manchego, then served on paprika-cinnamon dust with orange peel; makes 12, serving 4-6 as a main.
glance: 12 cakes, serving 4-6 as a main or 8-12 as an appetizer
2 cups short-grained Spanish paella rice with 3.5 cups broth, saffron and smoked paprika
2 eggs; the mixture should barely squeeze into a patty
3 teaspoons smoked paprika mixed with 1 teaspoon cinnamon
Vegetarian; gluten-free if you omit the breadcrumbs
faq: Why does smoked paprika with cinnamon work?

Mem of Vegetarian Duck introduced the author to the combination: rather than tasting like two spices it reads as a married, individual flavor. He uses about 3:1 paprika to cinnamon in savory dishes and the reverse in sweets.
What is a paella cake?

Technically a sketchy designation, but it conveys the idea of a Spanish rice flavored with saffron, formed into a patty. The crispy crust (socarrat) is made in the frying pan rather than while cooking the rice.
What went wrong the first time?

The cakes made for Thanksgiving didn't hold up well to reheating and lacked some flavor components; the next day the author dropped the fruit-vinegar reduction and added paprika and cinnamon, a slice of melting manchego and candied Seville orange peel, with much better results.
How do I shape the cakes?

Cool the rice (spread on a sheet tray in the fridge if hurried), mix in the beaten eggs so it just barely squeezes into a patty, press each patty into breadcrumbs on each side and fry gently shaped, not too thick, so the eggs set inside.
What can I substitute for Seville orange peel?
High-quality marmalade, and arborio rice if you can't find paella rice.

summary: Lightly cooked cherry tomato and ricotta bruschetta: halved cherry tomatoes warmed 2 minutes in garlic oil until half sauce, half salad, spooned over thick grilled pain au levain spread with room-temperature ricotta and topped with basil; makes 4 large pieces.
glance: 2 1/2 cups halved cherry tomatoes cooked about 2 minutes with garlic
4 thick slices pain au levain, brushed with olive oil and grilled until well browned
3/4 cup fresh ricotta at room temperature
faq: Why cook the tomatoes at all?

The author would usually do this bruschetta without cooking, just tossing them with the other ingredients ahead. But cooking just a couple of minutes makes the tomatoes break down into something halfway between salad and sauce that is quite luxurious with the ricotta.
Why thick bread?
Thick slices let you get nice browned flavors on the exterior while retaining a chewy interior crumb. Thin slices end up as a dry cracker. Artisan pain au levain brings chew and flavor.
How do I cook the tomatoes?

Saute minced garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil about 30 seconds, add the tomatoes and 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt and cook, stirring occasionally, about 2 minutes until warmed through and just starting to break down.
Which ricotta?
The author suggests Calabro, at room temperature.
Is the recipe exact?
It's approximate: the author didn't plan to share it, so use your own cooking sense to adjust.
